title: Draupadi falls first
hookLine: past the Himalayas, in a sea of sand, Draupadi falls, and Yudhishthira does not turn around
carry: dharma is subtle, and the epic lets us argue
tomorrow: the twins fall next, and the reason is one small sentence twice. what is it?

lines: A DESERT OF SAND, MERU AHEAD.
cards: Seven travelers climb into the Himalayas: five brothers, one queen, one dog. They cross the mountains and, beyond them, a great desert of sand, and far off they can see Meru, the mountain at the center of the world.
They walk in single file, Yudhishthira in front, Draupadi near the back. Then, without warning, she drops to the ground. Bhima sees her fall.
And the man at the front of the line keeps walking.

teach.b: Bhima calls out to his elder brother. In Ganguli's telling, his question is simple: she never did anything wrong, so why has she fallen? Yudhishthira answers without stopping.
She loved Arjuna more than the rest of us, he says. That is what she is paying for now. And he walks on, the text says, without looking at her.

teach.h: A HARD SENTENCE TO SIT WITH
teach.b: That's a hard sentence to sit with. Draupadi was dragged into the dice hall and humiliated. She lost her sons in the night raid.
And at the end of the road, the reason given is that her heart leaned toward one husband. Hear the echo.

teach.h: BHISHMA, IN THE DICE HALL: "DHARMA IS SUBTLE"
teach.b: In that dice hall, Draupadi asked the elders whether she had been lawfully staked, and Bhishma could only answer: the way of dharma is subtle.
The tradition calls it sukshma dharma, subtle dharma. Right action is hard to see, even good people carry small faults, and the epic often refuses to close a hard case.
So readers have argued about this verdict for centuries. Some hear the strict logic of the road. Some notice Yudhishthira never kneels, and ask what that costs him.

teach.h: HER FALL IS NOT THE LAST WORD
teach.b: And the tradition hasn't let her fall be the last word. The epic's final book shows Draupadi in heaven as Shri, the goddess of fortune, and in Tamil Nadu many villages worship her as Draupadi Amman.
Arguing with the story is how Hindus keep it alive. The brothers walk on. The dog keeps walking.

how: Draupadi's fall is told in the Mahaprasthanika Parva; Hindu readers and storytellers still argue over Yudhishthira's verdict, and Draupadi is worshipped as a goddess, Draupadi Amman, in many villages of Tamil Nadu.

games.q: the first fall — tap the pairs.

s: Yudhishthira stops and kneels beside Draupadi
the text says he walks on without looking at her.
Bhima is the one who asks why she fell
he calls out the question to his elder brother.
Draupadi's fall is the epic's last word on her
the last book shows her in heaven as Shri, and many in Tamil Nadu worship her as Draupadi Amman.

games.q: a classmate says the Mahabharata just tells you what's right and wrong. after Draupadi's fall, what fits?
o: not quite: it calls dharma subtle and leaves hard verdicts for readers to argue.
yes: every verdict in it is final.
no: it has no idea of right and wrong.
games.why: Bhishma told Draupadi in the dice hall that dharma is subtle. the epic gives Yudhishthira's verdict, Bhima's question and her honor in heaven, and lets readers argue.

practice: Let your breath slow and bring to mind someone who walked a long stretch of road with you and isn't with you anymore, for any reason.
Say their name silently, and instead of walking on, stop and stay with them for a few breaths, the way Bhima stopped to look.
If you pray, hold them in your prayer, or light a small lamp for them as many Hindus do; if you don't, just stay.
